brief: Goldman Sachs daily Asia digest. The lead macro change is that GS now expects a 25bp hike at the September FOMC, shifting from hold. It states an unchanged inflation view and no strong economic case, so the driver is credibility: the market prices a nearly 90% chance, and Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech, an imperfect CPI report and higher oil pressured the Fed, even as core PCE improves. Further hikes sit outside baseline. With the 10-year near 5%, GS still expects the equity bull market to continue, because long debt maturities limit balance sheet risk and tightening through mid-2027 is priced. In tech, China semi capex grows double-digit to US$82bn by 2030 on generative AI demand and localization, feeding local equipment, EDA, PMIC, GaN and specialty memory, with tight upstream components the constraint. Optical demand stays strong, 1.6T above US$700, though DSP, laser and PCB supply could cap 2027 shipments. The same AI export surge adds 7pp to Taiwan GDP. BHP Copper South Australia NPV rises to US$37bn on a 20% IRR. The $4,900 gold forecast assumes the Fed on hold. Dollar weakness persists as JPY and KRW join the CNY trend.
